pointers.needs: The shared anchors this volume relies on, declared as needs until shared/ lands

shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for forge.started 100; forge.snapshot 200; forge.recovered 200; forge.auth 400; forge.throttled 429; forge.overflow 500; forge.slow 500; forge.unreachable 503. Owner-acts: forge.auth; forge.overflow; forge.unreachable after three consecutive failed polls past forge.stale_after_seconds.

Entity forge:snapshot (main_sha, main_gate, prs[], hash, polled_at, stale, failed_since, etags) written every poll by compare-and-swap; table forge_history(seq, hash, polled_at, body JSON) appended on hash change.
Reconcile, not events: a poll of the forge is the correctness path; a webhook can only call poll_now and never writes state (S03 section 8 item 3, D06 C44).
No agent reads GitHub for state; one poller, one rate budget, one truth.
A seat pushes and opens its PR with its own gh under its rendered permissions (N-13); it never writes the snapshot and never reads the service token.

forge.poll_seconds 30, forge.request_seconds 10, forge.poll_budget_seconds 20, forge.calls_per_poll_max 60, forge.throttle_floor 1000, forge.throttle_max_seconds 900, forge.stale_after_seconds 180, forge.min_interval_seconds 5, forge.prs_max 200, forge.keep_days 30, forge.ticket_pattern; the read token in STATE/config/service.env as COQ_FORGE_READ_TOKEN.

Three request attempts fail: entity stale, forge.unreachable 503 once per transition, N-08 reads pending, N-09 holds, polls continue, one card after three failed polls past stale_after; forge.recovered 200 on the first success.

purpose.is: N-04 is the one place the factory learns what GitHub holds: open pull requests with their head shas, the coq/gate status on each head and on main, mergeability, and the main sha. It polls on every poll tick (D06, C44) and writes one forge.snapshot the gate (N-08), the merge (N-09) and the main verdict (N-10) read.

Correctness never depends on a delivery: GitHub does not redeliver a failed webhook, so the poll is the correctness path and a webhook can only ever make it faster (S01 section 5, I03 F3: events make it fast, reconciliation makes it true).
purpose.is-not: It does not post statuses (N-25 does, from Jenkins), does not merge (N-09), does not decide a verdict (N-08), and holds no second copy of GitHub beyond the latest snapshot and its history in the store.
purpose.decisions: D06 (poll each tick, webhooks later as accelerators), D05 (the verdict is the coq/gate status on the commit), D18 (GitHub now, Forgejo later: the forge client is an interface with one implementation).

record.field: forge.poll_seconds from config (30 by default; the ci/README.md Jenkins poll proved 0.37 s per check, so 30 s is latency, not load).

also.note: arrive at GitHub, not here; the poll reads them; drawn as the N-25 to N-04 edge

also.from: N-09 after a merge and N-16 after a push
also.note: an accelerator: one extra poll at once, bounded by forge.min_interval_seconds 5; never required for correctness

record.field: The coq/gate status on main_sha: success, failure, error, pending, none, with its target url and description.

One entry per open PR: number, head_sha, head_ref, base_ref, mergeable (true, false, unknown), gate (coq/gate on head_sha with state, target url, description, updated_at), gate_page (coq/gate-page when present), draft, ticket (parsed from the branch name or title by the pattern in config), labels.
sha256 of the canonical body without at, so unchanged polls compare equal.
false on a fresh poll; the entity (not the record) carries stale true with age when polls fail.

output.rule: Write-if-changed (S03 section 8 item 2): the snapshot entity forge:snapshot is written every poll (version grows, polled_at moves); the forge.snapshot record is appended only when hash changes. Readers that need "is it fresh" read the entity; readers that need "what changed" read the records.
output.record: Three attempts failed; the entity is marked stale with the first failure time; readers treat a stale snapshot older than forge.stale_after_seconds 180 as pending (N-08) and hold merges (N-09).
GitHub rate limit hit; the poll backs off to the reset time GitHub reports, at most forge.throttle_max_seconds 900.
The token is missing, expired or lacks scope; one card through N-28; polling continues and keeps failing until fixed, so the lamp stays red.

mechanism.component: Go package scheduler/internal/forge: an interface Forge with ListOpenPRs, Statuses(sha), Ref(name), and one implementation for GitHub over REST v3 with conditional requests; a fake in testkit answers from fixtures. The Forgejo implementation is a later ticket against the same interface (D18, C55).

A fine-grained GitHub token with contents:read, pull_requests:read, statuses:read on the one repository, read from the unit's EnvironmentFile STATE/config/service.env (mode 0600, never in the repository, never in a record; D03 C37: subscription for seats, keys only for machines).

Per poll: GET repos/O/R/git/ref/heads/main (1), GET repos/O/R/pulls?state=open&per_page=100 (1 per page), GET repos/O/R/commits/SHA/status for main and for each open PR head whose head_sha changed or whose last gate was pending (N). ETag and If-None-Match on every GET so an unchanged list costs no rate limit (304).

forge.calls_per_poll_max 60; over the budget the poll stops after main and the PR list, marks the rest "statuses deferred", and the next poll continues from where it stopped in PR number order. The primary limit is 5000 per hour; at 30 s and 60 calls the worst case is 7200, so the budget halves to 30 automatically when remaining is under 1000 (forge.throttle_floor).
mechanism.mermaid: flowchart LR T[poll tick N-06] --> M[GET ref main, ETag] M --> P[GET open PRs, ETag] P --> S{heads changed or gate pending?} S -- yes --> C[GET status per head, budgeted] S -- no --> H C --> H[canonical body, hash] H --> E[entity forge:snapshot CAS write] E --> D{hash changed?} D -- yes --> R[append forge.snapshot 200] D -- no --> X[counter forge.unchanged] R --> N8[N-08 gate check]
mechanism.step: Read the previous entity forge:snapshot (version v) for ETags and last hashes.
Fetch main ref; fetch open PRs page by page up to forge.prs_max 200 (more is forge.overflow 500 and the first 200 by number).

For each PR whose head_sha differs from the last snapshot, or whose last gate state was pending or none, or whose mergeable was unknown: fetch the combined status; copy coq/gate and coq/gate-page contexts only (ci/README.md status table, kept); other contexts are ignored.
Parse ticket id from head_ref by forge.ticket_pattern (WO-YYYYMMDD-xxxx) else from the title; absent is null, never guessed.
Build the body, canonical JSON, hash; CAS-write the entity with expected_version v; on 409 (another poll committed first, which only happens after a restart overlap) re-read and give up this tick.
Append forge.snapshot 200 when hash changed; the record is what N-08 consumes (one gate.verdict per PR head per change).
Mergeable unknown on GitHub means its background job has not run; the poll asks again next tick; N-09 never merges on unknown.
mechanism.accelerator: Webhooks later (D06 "A later"): a listener would only call forge.poll_now; it never writes the snapshot itself, so a lost or forged delivery changes nothing but timing. Until then, N-09 and N-16 call poll_now after their own pushes.

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. The poll runs on the poll tick N-06 emits from the service's own clock; the first poll runs at start as soon as the store is open and the token is read.
start.step: At start, read the token from the environment the unit passed; missing or empty is forge.auth 400 once and the poll keeps trying every tick with the same report latched (one record per transition, not per tick).
Load the previous entity for ETags; a missing entity means a cold full poll with no conditional headers.
forge.started 100 with the remaining rate limit the first response reported.

wait.name: http
wait.fallback: counts as a failed attempt; see retries

wait.name: poll-total
wait.fallback: the poll stops where it is, writes what it has with statuses deferred, and the next tick continues; forge.slow 500 once per transition

wait.name: rate-limit
wait.timeout: the reset time, at most forge.throttle_max_seconds 900
wait.fallback: forge.throttled 429; the entity is stale after forge.stale_after_seconds; N-08 reads pending and N-09 holds; nothing loops

wait.name: mergeable
wait.timeout: none held: unknown is a value
wait.fallback: asked again next tick; N-09 treats unknown as not yet

wait.name: store
wait.fallback: 503, retried per retries; the next tick overwrites anyway

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports.
retries.step: A 5xx, a timeout or a connection error is retried 3 times with 2, 4, 8 s inside the poll budget; the fourth failure ends the poll as failed.

A failed poll marks the entity stale (stale true, failed_since) and appends forge.unreachable 503 once per transition; polls continue every tick; the first success appends forge.recovered 200 with the outage length. Three consecutive failed polls plus stale over forge.stale_after_seconds is the owner-acts condition N-28 turns into one card, because a dark CI path was RC7's silent failure.
Not retried inside the poll: back off to the reset time; forge.throttled 429 once; the budget floor halves the calls per poll until remaining recovers.
Not retried: forge.auth 400 once; one card; the poll keeps running so recovery is automatic when the token is fixed.

many-agents.reading: Every gate, merge and verdict node and every screen reads the one snapshot entity or its records; twenty readers see one version each; nobody calls GitHub for state except this node (one poller means one rate budget and one truth; L02 section 8 item 6: GitHub is the one place every merge shows up).
many-agents.working: Seats push branches and open PRs through their own gh calls in their run (N-16); they never write the snapshot; what they did shows up in the next poll.
many-agents.collision: The service restarts while a poll is in flight, or a second instance is started by hand: the entity CAS on version admits one writer; the other gets 409 and stops. The unit's single instance (N-06, systemd) makes this a restart edge case, not a steady state.

N-16 pushes a new head while the poll reads statuses: the snapshot may hold the old head with its gate and the PR list with the new head; the hash changes next tick and N-08 issues a new verdict for the new head; the old head's verdict is superseded by sha, never reused (gate.sh heads_match predicate, L01 section 8 item 4, kept as code in N-08).
Jenkins posts ERROR superseded on the old sha and pending on the new one (ci/README.md): both are copied as they are; N-08 keys verdicts by head_sha so neither overwrites the other.
Ten seats call poll_now within a second: forge.min_interval_seconds collapses them into one poll; the rest return the in-flight poll's result.
many-agents.test: Fixture forge with 50 PRs, two of them changing heads every tick, one with gate flapping, and a scripted 429 at tick 7 and a 500 storm at tick 12: the snapshot records equal the fixture's change list exactly, the entity goes stale at tick 12 plus three attempts and recovers at tick 15, the rate budget never exceeds the floor during the 429.

owner, one card from N-28 (fix the token in service.env)

path.writer: the owner, once, by the runbook; read by the unit

reads-by.note: N-09's input edge is drawn from N-08; it reads the entity for mergeability

actor.name: N-04 in-process
actor.may: read GitHub with the read-only token; write the forge entity and records

actor.name: seat (the model)
actor.may: nothing here; it uses its own gh in its run for pushes and PR creation under its rendered permissions (N-13)

actor.name: pod
actor.may: nothing here; statuses come from Jenkins' own credential (N-25)

actor.name: owner
actor.may: write STATE/config/service.env once; rotate the token; `scheduler ctl forge get` to read the snapshot

permissions.rule: The token is read-only on one repository; the merge (N-09) uses a separate token with contents:write held by the same env file under another name, so a bug here can never write to GitHub.

monitoring.surface: Map screen (N-38) shows the forge as a machine with a lamp (fresh, stale, dark); Stats (N-40) shows rate remaining; Alerts (N-41) shows forge.unreachable and forge.auth.

runbook.task: `scheduler ctl forge get` prints main sha, main gate, every open PR with head and gate state, polled_at and stale.
`scheduler ctl forge poll` calls poll_now; it is bounded by min_interval and never needed for correctness.

Create a fine-grained token with contents:read, pull_requests:read, statuses:read on the repository; write COQ_FORGE_READ_TOKEN=... into STATE/config/service.env (0600); `systemctl --user restart coq-service`; confirm forge.started shows remaining.
The card names the env file and this task; nothing else is needed.

item.what: public ingress for webhooks (option A) and outbound forwarders or ARC runners (option B) as the correctness path
item.reason: C44 ruled the poll; GitHub does not redeliver a missed delivery; A stays allowed later only as an accelerator that calls poll_now

item.what: a 60 s bash poll of merged PRs that self-exits after 7 days with flock
item.reason: K12: a bash loop as control plane died silently; this node is a goroutine of the one unit with a stale lamp and a latched report

item.what: the webhook listener as the write path for gate verdicts
item.reason: RC7: the CI verdict path was dark end to end and nothing said so; the poll reads the status GitHub holds, and a webhook can only accelerate

item.what: T11 webhook redelivery reconciler (list deliveries, redeliver non-OK within 3 days)
item.reason: deferred with the webhook itself; when the accelerator lands, T11 is its own ticket under this node
the records tree is gone (N-01); the only poll left is this one against the forge, and its interval is 30 s because the forge is the slow external

item.what: Argo CD polling as the way GitHub state reaches the cluster
item.reason: Argo's poll is about gitops manifests (N-20, N-21, N-35); it is not the factory's view of PRs and statuses
